title: Principle-based Dataflow Optimization for Communication Lower Bound in Operator-Fused Tensor Accelerator
problem: Design space exploration for tensor accelerator dataflows is time-consuming and lacks architectural insight; optimal memory communication bounds for fused operators are not well characterized.
motivation: Tensor accelerators require efficient dataflow to minimize memory bandwidth which is a critical bottleneck; principled optimization replaces expensive DSE.
method: Proposes principles for dataflow optimization that provide communication lower bounds for tensor operators; derives optimal tiling, scheduling, mapping for intra/inter-operator dataflow; introduces FuseCU architecture supporting profitable operator fusion.
key_novelty: First principle-based approach to determine communication lower bounds for tensor dataflows; identifies all profitable operator fusions for memory communication savings.
contributions: Dataflow optimization principles providing communication lower bounds
Optimal tiling, scheduling, and mapping derivation
Identification of profitable tensor-wise operator fusions
FuseCU architecture for profitable fusion support
63.6% data movement saving vs TPUv4i, 1.33x speedup, open-sourced

metrics.speedup: 1.33x vs TPUv4i, 1.25x vs Gemmini, 1.14x vs Planaria

primary_theme: principle-based dataflow optimization with operator fusion
